security.groupsAttributeHint: Name of the assertion attribute that lists the groups. Entra ID: http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/claims/groups (group object IDs).

security.scimDesc: Accounts, roles and deactivation pushed by your identity provider

dataCheck.title: Check my data
dataCheck.description: Runs the query the scheduled analysis sends, one filter at a time, against your log store, and shows where logs drop out.
dataCheck.fixFailed: The change could not be saved.
dataCheck.noPermission: Ask someone who can use integrations to run the check.
dataCheck.steps: What the scheduled analysis would find (last {{minutes}} min)

step.title: Step
step.services: From the services this project lists

reason.no_services: The project lists no services, so no logs are analysed. Add a service.
reason.no_log_provider: No active log integration. Connect one in Settings → Observability.
reason.no_log_location: No index, log group or stream with logs for this project was found. Set where your logs are in the log integration, or run Check my data.
reason.logs_not_tagged: Logs are arriving in the log store, but none in the window carry this project's tag (project_name or a project rule), so nothing could be analysed. Run Check my data to see the values your logs carry.
reason.no_matching_logs: The log store returned no error or warning logs for this project and environment. That is good news if nothing failed; if your services did log errors, run Check my data.
reason.already_analysed: Every log found was already part of an earlier analysis.
reason.outside_window: The logs found carry timestamps outside the analysis window.
reason.not_important: The logs found were not errors or warnings.
reason.other_environment: The logs found belong to another environment.
reason.quiet: Errors and warnings were at their usual level, so no analysis was needed.

diagnosis.no_log_provider: No active log integration. Connect one in Settings → Observability.
diagnosis.no_log_location: SerOps found no index, log group or stream with logs for this project. Set where your logs are in the log integration (index pattern or log groups).
diagnosis.no_logs: The log store has no logs at all in the last {{minutes}} minutes in the places this project reads from. Check that your shipper is running and sending to this store.
diagnosis.project_not_tagged: Logs are arriving, but none carry project_name = “{{project}}”. Add that field (or label, or tag) to your logs in the shipper; the values your logs carry today are listed below.
diagnosis.environment_not_tagged: Logs for this project are arriving, but none carry the environment “{{environment}}” or one of its spellings. Use a value your logs carry, or tag the logs with this environment.
diagnosis.errors_unreadable: Logs reach SerOps and are tagged correctly, but the error query found nothing while {{count}} of the sampled lines read like errors or warnings. Level fields SerOps does not read: {{fields}}. Name the level field log_level, level or severity (or relabel it in the shipper) so errors are analysed.
diagnosis.no_errors: Logs reach SerOps and are tagged correctly. There were no errors or warnings in the last {{minutes}} minutes, so there was nothing to analyse. That is good news.
diagnosis.no_services: Errors and warnings are arriving, but the project lists no services yet. List the services below to analyse them.
diagnosis.unregistered_services: Errors and warnings are arriving, but only from services this project does not list. List them to analyse them.
diagnosis.ok: Everything is in place: {{count}} errors and warnings would be analysed now.

welcomeStep.title: Welcome to SerOps
welcomeStep.intro: Let's connect your first AI model and log source so we can run your first analysis. The wizard watches your workspace as you go — no need to confirm each step.

aiProviderStep.title: Choose your AI model
aiProviderStep.intro: SerOps supports Gemini, Claude, OpenAI, DeepSeek, and Ollama (local). Pick one and add your key — we'll encrypt it at rest and use it for every batch analysis.

observabilityStep.title: Connect an observability source
observabilityStep.intro: Point SerOps at your log store (Elasticsearch, Loki, Datadog, CloudWatch…). We'll pull recent logs into every batch analysis. Metrics are optional for the same provider.

createProjectStep.title: Create your first project
createProjectStep.intro: A project is a grouping of services SerOps analyzes together — e.g. "Payments Backend" or "Data Pipeline". Default environments (development, staging, production) are created for you.

linkServiceStep.title: Link a service
linkServiceStep.introBefore: Tell us the name of a service in your project (e.g.
linkServiceStep.introAfter: ). As soon as you add it, we'll kick off your first analysis in the background.

scmStep.title: Connect source control (optional)
scmStep.intro: Link a repository so AI can correlate incidents with recent commits. You can skip this and add it later from Settings.

cicdStep.title: Connect CI/CD (optional)
cicdStep.intro: Link a build or deploy pipeline so AI can correlate incidents with recent deployments. You can skip this and add it later from Settings.
